purpose: Style guidance for invented demo floorplans; not verified campus plans.

inspection.method: All four original images visually inspected with view_image; dominant raster colors sampled to distinguish photographed blue cast from intended diagram palette.
inspection.measurement_caveat: Stroke and font sizes are practical visual estimates; palette below is a clean rendering target, not exact photographic color recovery.

palette.notes: Use one flat navy fill across rooms and circulation. Pale blue walls and nearly white labels provide contrast. Photographs contain deeper saturated blues, lavender surroundings, light streaks, and moire; do not reproduce those artifacts.

rendering.units: Pixels at a reference canvas approximately 750 px wide; scale linearly with output width.
rendering.effects: Flat diagram; no shadows, gradients, textures, perspective, or decorative furniture.
rendering.silhouette_rule: Parent supplies the exact original-source silhouette mask. Clip every fill, wall, door, symbol, and label to that mask; do not infer or redraw the footprint from these style references.
rendering.boundary_rule: Draw the perimeter inside the mask so the outside extent remains exact. Interior walls may meet the perimeter but must not create protrusions.

typography.alignment: Centered within each room or corridor segment, usually horizontal; a few narrow service labels may be vertical if necessary.
typography.label_background: None; reserve navy clearance around text and avoid wall crossings.
typography.notes: Compact bold or semibold white sans-serif numerals. Labels are functional and numerous; no titles inside the footprint. Floor 3 reference has visibly larger labels than the denser lower floors.

numbering.room_rule: Floor 0 uses unpadded one- or two-digit room numbers. Floors 1, 2, and 3 use the floor digit followed by two room digits. Append an uppercase letter for related subdivisions; keep labels unique per floor.
numbering.notes: Assign corridor numbers by connected segment and stairs by persistent vertical core. Floor 2 reference has very few visible circulation labels; use them sparingly in its open areas.

doors.symbol: Break the partition at the opening; draw one thin hinged leaf and one quarter-circle swing arc in the wall color.
doors.placement: Open rooms onto adjacent circulation. Mix left and right hinges. Put double opposing swing leaves at major entrances or wide rooms.
doors.density: Typically one door per room; repeat doors rhythmically on corridor-facing partitions, not on every wall.
doors.notes: At this scale some doors read as a small rounded notch. Preserve clean openings and arcs without making the symbol heavier than walls.

stairs_and_services.stair_symbol: Small rectangular core with thin parallel pale blue treads, sometimes two flights around a dark landing; add a bright cyan directional arrow or block on the flight.
stairs_and_services.stair_label_placement: Inside the core or immediately beside it, without covering treads where space allows.
stairs_and_services.secondary_symbols: Occasional narrow rectangles with diagonal X braces for shafts or service voids; tiny lift cores beside circulation.
stairs_and_services.optional_reference_markers: References show pink circular lift icons and small yellow restroom/accessibility pictograms. These are secondary; avoid making them a dominant palette element.

spatial_composition.shared: Mostly orthogonal partitions, straight corridor spines with short branches, repeated perimeter rooms, compact service clusters, and a few larger rooms. Preserve each target building's exact silhouette rather than transferring the reference building outline.

floor_0.organization: Branching circulation joins several wings; large room blocks alternate with clusters of small letter-suffixed support rooms. Multiple stairs sit at peripheral ends and one sits nearer the center.
floor_0.visual_character: Irregular room rhythm, many corridor segment labels, several broad rooms, tightly packed services near the main circulation junction.

floor_1.organization: Connected corridor network with repeated small perimeter offices and larger central rooms. Fine subdivisions form dense service or office clusters; outer wings retain some larger room blocks.
floor_1.visual_character: Many letter suffixes, frequent door arcs, narrow spaces, strong circulation continuity.

floor_2.density: Low, with most of the interior left open.
floor_2.organization: A small central room cluster and scattered isolated rooms sit within broad navy open areas. A few peripheral stairs and service shafts anchor the layout.
floor_2.visual_character: Sparse partitions and labels, large uninterrupted navy fields, limited enclosed rooms. Do not densely tile this floor.

floor_3.organization: Long horizontal corridors connect side circulation spines. Rows of similarly sized rectangular rooms flank the corridors, with a few larger central rooms and stair cores near edges and junctions.
floor_3.visual_character: Repeated room widths, frequent inward door swings, larger readable numerals, a small number of clearly labeled corridor runs.

review_checks: All geometry remains inside the exact parent-provided silhouette mask.
Rooms and corridors share a flat navy fill with thin pale boundaries.
White labels remain readable and do not collide with partitions or door arcs.
Room numbers match floor 0, 1, 2, or 3; corridor and stair identifiers follow the corresponding floor prefix.
Stair treads are visible and cyan accents identify stairs consistently.
Floor 2 remains distinctly more open than floors 0, 1, and 3.
Demo status is recorded in metadata or captions outside the floorplan artwork.
